questions.accessible_text:
1. [Maximum mark: 4]

The second term of an arithmetic sequence is 10 and the fourth term is 22.

(a) Find the value of the common difference. [2]

(b) Find an expression for uₙ, the nth term. [2]
questions.summary: Find an arithmetic sequence’s common difference and nth term.
questions.solution: u₄−u₂=2d=12, so d=6. Then u₁=10−6=4 and uₙ=4+6(n−1)=6n−2.

questions.accessible_text:
2. [Maximum mark: 6]

Claire rolls a six-sided die 16 times. The scores are shown in the frequency table.

[Table: Score 1, 2, 3, 4, 5, 6; frequency p, q, 4, 2, 0, 3 respectively.]

The mean score is 3.

(a) Find p and q. [5]

Each score is multiplied by 10 to determine a final score.

(b) Write down the mean final score. [1]
questions.summary: Find missing frequencies and transform a mean.
questions.solution: (a) Total frequency: p+q=7. Total score 48: p+2q+12+8+18=48, so p+2q=10. Hence p=4, q=3. (b) The mean becomes 10×3=30.

3. [Maximum mark: 5]

It is given that log₁₀a=1/3, where a>0. Find

(a) log₁₀(1/a); [2]

(b) log₁₀₀₀a. [3]
questions.summary: Apply logarithm laws and change of base.

questions.accessible_text:
4. [Maximum mark: 8]

Points A and B lie on a circle of radius r cm centred at O. Sector OAB has central angle θ radians.

[Diagram, not to scale: sector OAB with OA=OB=r cm and angle AÔB=θ.]

The sector perimeter is 10 cm and its area is 6.25 cm².

(a) Show that 4r²−20r+25=0. [4]

(b) Hence, or otherwise, find r and θ. [4]
questions.summary: Use sector perimeter and area equations.
questions.solution: 2r+rθ=10 and r²θ/2=6.25. Eliminating θ gives 6.25=r(10−2r)/2, hence 4r²−20r+25=0. Thus (2r−5)²=0, r=5/2 cm, and θ=(10−2r)/r=2.

questions.accessible_text:
5. [Maximum mark: 7]

Consider f(x)=cos x and g(x)=sin2x, where 0≤x≤π. Their graphs intersect at A, B=(π/2,0), and C.

[Diagram: f is a decreasing cosine curve and g is one full sine arch on 0≤x≤π. They intersect at A in the first quadrant, B=(π/2,0), and C in the fourth quadrant. Region R between the curves from B to C is shaded.]

(a) Find the x-coordinates of A and C. [3]

(b) Find the area of R. [4]
questions.summary: Find trigonometric intersections and an enclosed area.
questions.solution: sin2x=2sin x cos x. Besides cos x=0 at B, sin x=1/2 gives x_A=π/6 and x_C=5π/6. Area=∫_{π/2}^{5π/6}(cos x−sin2x)dx=[sin x+(1/2)cos2x]=1/4.

6. [Maximum mark: 5]

A geometric sequence has first term 1 and common ratio 10. Sₙ is the sum of its first n terms.

(a) Find Sₙ in the form (aⁿ−1)/b, where a,b∈ℤ⁺. [1]

(b) Hence show that S₁+S₂+⋯+Sₙ=[10(10ⁿ−1)−9n]/81. [4]
questions.summary: Sum a geometric sequence and its partial sums.

7. [Maximum mark: 14]

Consider y=x³−x²−x+1.

(a) Find (i) dy/dx; (ii) d²y/dx². [3]

The curve has a local maximum at A.

(b) Find A, using part (a)(ii) to justify your answer. [6]

The curve has a point of inflexion at B.

(c) Find the x-coordinate of B. [2]

L is the normal at (0,1).

(d) Find the equation of L. [3]
questions.summary: Analyze a cubic and its normal.
questions.solution: (a) y′=3x²−2x−1; y″=6x−2. (b) y′=(3x+1)(x−1), and y″(−1/3)=−4<0, so A=(−1/3,32/27). (c) y″=0 gives x=1/3. (d) Tangent slope at x=0 is −1, so normal slope is 1 and L: y=x+1.

questions.accessible_text:
8. [Maximum mark: 14]

Let f(x)=(4x+2)/(x−2), x≠2.

(a) Sketch y=f(x), indicating axis intercepts and labelling asymptotes. [5]

(b) Write down the range of f. [1]

Let g(x)=x²+bx+c. Its axis of symmetry is x=2 and its roots are −1/2 and p, where p∈ℚ.

(c) Show p=9/2. [1]

(d) Find b and c. [3]

(e) Find the y-coordinate of the vertex of y=g(x). [2]

(f) Find the number of solutions of f(x)=g(x). [2]
questions.solution: (a) f=4+10/(x−2): asymptotes x=2, y=4; intercepts (−1/2,0), (0,−1), with branches above-right and below-left of (2,4). (b) y≠4. (c) (−1/2+p)/2=2, so p=9/2. (d) g=(x+1/2)(x−9/2)=x²−4x−9/4, so b=−4,c=−9/4. (e) g(2)=−25/4. (f) There are 3 intersections.

9. [Maximum mark: 17]

A bag initially contains three red and one blue button. Francine selects one button, replaces it, and adds one extra button of the same colour, then selects a second button.

[Tree: first red 3/4, blue 1/4; after red, second red 4/5 and blue 1/5; after blue, second red p and blue q.]

(a) Find p and q. [2]

(b) Show that P(two of the same colour)=7/10. [2]

(c) Given two of the same colour, find P(two red). [3]

Let X be the number of red buttons selected.

[Distribution table: x=0,1,2; P(X=x)=1/10,a,b.]

(d) Find a and b. [2]

(e) Find E(X). [2]

Francine restarts and repeats until selecting blue.

(f) Given the first two selections are red, write down P(next is blue). [1]

P(the first blue is after n selections in total)=3/56.

(g) Find n. [5]
questions.summary: Apply conditional probability to a reinforced process.
